## Added

- New `model` command: a deterministic, storey-by-storey 3D reconstruction
  from a CAD-exported drawing set — the Rust port of the earlier
  prototype. Walls, the building envelope and the rooms are read off the
  plan sheets by fill colour, storeys are stacked on the printed grid axes,
  openings are what the envelope minus rooms minus walls leaves (edge pieces
  are glazing, interior pieces door gaps), ground-floor wall pieces outside
  the envelope are the stone piers, terrace edges become railings, the roof
  plan gives the roof outline and a parapet ring. Output: `model.json` (2D
  polygons with z ranges, metres about the grid origin), a binary glTF
  (`.glb`, per-vertex colours, Z up), and a map-native extruded
  FeatureCollection (`height` / `base` / `color` per feature, the same shape
  `building` emits). On the reference document every polygon matches the
  prototype's output to within 0.1 % of its area.
- `model` **detects its parameters from the document**: which sheets are the
  floor plans and the roof plan (title blocks), the plan scale, the storey
  levels (titles), the parapet level, slab thickness and plinth (level marks
  on the elevations and section), the fill colours (the plan's own fills)
  and the grid labels (the lettered bubbles). Every decision is listed in
  `params_notes`. `--params <file>` overrides detection with a reviewed file
  (the `params` block of a previous run); `--llm-params [MODEL]` asks a
  hosted model (`gemini-3.8-flash` by default) to confirm or correct them —
  the proposal is checked against the drawings before use and falls back to
  detection with a warning. Networked, opt-in, like every model call.
- `model` **places the reconstruction on the map** when the dossier allows:
  the ground-floor envelope is matched by shape to the building box drawn on
  a georeferenced sibling sheet (the site plan placed from its table, a
  sibling's, or `--parcel`), and the sheet's other line work settles which
  way round a symmetric box stands. `--georeference` references place it
  where the caller says. Otherwise the model stays in `local_metres`, right
  in shape and unknown in position, for a map to let someone put it down by
  hand — `georeference` reports which happened, with residuals.
- Page classification reads the **title block**: `classification.features`
  gains `sheet_title`, `sheet_role` (`floor_plan`, `roof_plan`, `elevation`,
  `section`, `site_plan`, `situation_plan`, `fence`, `views3d`,
  `sheet_index`), `sheet_level_m`, `level_marks` and `filled_paths`. A
  titled drawing is classified from its title with `certain` confidence; an
  untitled drawing with four or more level marks is an
  `elevation_or_section` (ambiguous). On the corpus this turns the floor
  plans, roof plans, elevations, sections and site plans that were
  `unknown` into their classes.
- `classification.class` gains **`roof_plan`**: a drawing, not mappable,
  vector. `dossier` labels carry it as before (`roof_plan` was already in
  the label vocabulary).
- Text recovery for CAD exports whose `Identity-H` fonts carry no
  `ToUnicode` map but use Unicode code points as CIDs (ArchiCAD): the
  content-stream interpreter now decodes such runs, so their title blocks,
  level marks and grid labels are readable by `vector`, `dossier` and
  `model`. Only Latin, Cyrillic, Armenian, Greek and common symbols are
  accepted, so a real glyph-indexed font yields little rather than noise.
- **`llm_usage[]` on every networked command**: `building`, `cadfix`,
  `dossier --vlm` and `model --llm-params` report each hosted call with its
  `label`, `model`, `provider`, `input_tokens` / `cached_input_tokens` /
  `output_tokens`, `elapsed_ms` and the `cost_usd` estimated from
  `models.json` — the figures the stderr `llm:` lines already printed, now in
  the contract so a caller can account for them. `docs/json-api.md`,
  *Token usage*.
- Two `pdf-geometry` examples for tuning another office's export:
  `page_fills` (fill colours and text sizes of a page) and `page_fonts`
  (font encodings and raw text operands).

## Changed

- `building` retries a reply that made no `add_part` call, up to three
  attempts, quoting the previous reply and insisting on the main building;
  each empty attempt is a `warnings` entry and the run fails only when all
  three came back empty.

- Workspace version 0.10.0: additive contract changes (`model`, the new
  `classification` fields and class value). Consumers pin the version.
- The reviewed dossier annotations (`data/annotations/*.json`) were
  regenerated: the only differences are the classification improvements
  above (`unknown` → the titled class) and `stats.placed_pages` where a
  page's class changed nothing else.
